_readme: Hole coordinates. Record these with tools/map-course.html while walking the course, then paste the exported JSON over the 'holes' array below and set 'mapped' to true.
_example: This is NOT the club's course. It is a real one — Pebble Beach Golf Links — standing in so the map and the yardages can be seen working on a genuine layout with genuine distances. 'mapped' stays false, which keeps the “course not mapped yet” banner up, the “Example layout” watermark on the map, and par off the scorecard. Replace the whole 'holes' array with the real course before setting 'mapped' to true.
_source: Hole centre-lines and green outlines from OpenStreetMap, © OpenStreetMap contributors, made available under the Open Database Licence (ODbL) — https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright. Tee is the first node of each golf=hole way; centre is the centroid of the matching golf=green polygon; front and back are that polygon's nearest and furthest vertices from the tee. 'cardYards' is measured tee to green centre, so it differs by a few yards from the printed card, which measures to the championship tee and along the line of play.
_note: Each hole can carry a 'note': local knowledge that no commercial app has for this course — where the trouble is, what the wind does, which side to miss on. Written once by someone who knows the course, and worth more than any yardage. The mapper does not collect these; add them by hand and keep them to one or two sentences.

holes.note: Downhill and barely a wedge, but it plays straight into the ocean wind. Short and left is sand; long is the Pacific.
The second shot is over a cliff inlet. There is no bail-out long — take the yardage to the front and trust it.
The sea runs down the entire left side. Everything you miss right is recoverable; nothing you miss left is.

_path: 'path' is the hole's centre-line: the route the hole actually takes, tee first. Two points for a straight par 3, more where the hole doglegs. The map draws it, which is what makes one hole look different from another — without it every hole renders as a tee at the bottom and a green at the top. It is optional: a hole with no 'path' falls back to a straight line from tee to green centre.
_bunkers: 'bunkers' is a list of sand rings, each a closed outline of 4-6 points. They are drawn on the single-hole map only: at whole-course scale a hundred of them is noise, not information. Simplified hard on purpose — the vertex budget scales with the bunker's perimeter (5 points for a pot bunker, up to 12 for a waste area), because a fixed budget leaves big bunkers looking like spikes and small ones carrying detail no player can see. Optional: a hole without the field simply draws no sand.
